questions.q: Which conditions are both needed for iron to rust?
questions.why: Iron only rusts when both oxygen (air) and water are present; barrier methods exclude both.

questions.q: Why does zinc protect steel from rusting even when the zinc coating is scratched?
options: Zinc is less reactive than iron so it does not corrode
Zinc forms an alloy with iron
Zinc is more reactive, so it loses electrons more readily than iron
Zinc gains electrons from the iron
questions.why: Sacrificial protection: zinc is oxidised (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻) instead of the iron.

questions.q: Which pollutant is matched with its source?
options: carbon monoxide: incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels
methane: complete combustion of fossil fuels
oxides of nitrogen: decomposition of vegetation
questions.why: CO comes from incomplete combustion; methane from vegetation and animal digestion; NOₓ from car engines; SO₂ from burning fuels containing sulfur.

questions.q: Explain, in terms of structure, why an alloy is harder and stronger than the pure metal.
questions.model: The alloy contains atoms of different sizes, which disrupt the regular layers, so the layers can no longer slide over each other.
points: layers can no longer slide over each other
